subject: Agree migration lanes, customer notice timing, and exemption criteria — Infer-V2 rollout
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Agree migration lanes, customer notice timing, and exemption criteria — Infer-V2 rollout

Team —

Following last week's leadership sync, we need to lock down three things for the Infer-V2 phaseout:

1) Migration lanes and the gating criteria for each lane (auto-migrate vs manual opt-in vs long-tail exemption).
2) Customer notice schedule and the public-facing FAQ draft.
3) Exception policy: what constitutes an allowable exemption, who approves, and what telemetry/signoffs we require.

What I'm proposing (quick, please review inline):
- Timeline: initial customer notice on 2028-06-01, targeted auto-migration window 2028-07-01 to 2028-09-01, long-tail exemption window until 2029-01-01.
- Exemption policy (draft): technical incompatibility (model architecture/latency > 200ms at 95th), contractual restrictions, or regulatory constraints — exceptions limited to 8–12 customers per quarter and require PM + Eng approval + legal review.
- Communications: 3-burst cadence (pre-notice, migration start, 30-day reminder) + onboarding guide and runbook for customers who opt-in early.

Asks for this thread:
- Aditya: can the compatibility shim cover customers on custom tokenizers or with <8k context? If not, propose alternatives and the expected engineering effort (FTE estimate).
- Marissa: can you draft the public FAQ & the customer notice (I attached a starting draft)?
- Laura: ops ownership for scheduling the comms and locking the migration blackout windows (I included a proposed schedule in the spreadsheet).

I'll compile decisions into the migration matrix once we have answers. Please reply with decided items or objections by EOD Friday 2028-05-19 so we can announce next Monday.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Agree migration lanes, customer notice timing, and exemption criteria — Infer-V2 rollout

Ben — thanks for the clear asks. Quick technical clarifications and constraints from Product/Platform: 

- Compatibility shim: we can cover most tokenizer differences via a conversion layer for text-only workloads. Differences that break structured outputs (function-calling schemas) or custom tokenizers used with embedding hooks are higher risk. For context lengths: a trimmed-prefix strategy will work for customers under 12k; under 2k we need to validate behavioral regression tests.

- Engineering effort: to deliver a robust compatibility shim + a regression suite (10 representative customer prompts + synthetic edge cases) we estimate ~1.5 engineer-months (1 SWE + 0.5 test engineer) for the initial ship, plus ~0.5 eng-month recurring for support during the migration window. If we need to support custom tokenizers as a first-class migration path, add ~2–3 engineer-months and a small library change.

- Exceptions: Product is comfortable with a small, controlled exception bucket (<=10 customers per quarter) if we require:
  * documented reproduction in our staging environment,
  * a short-term SLA tweak (if needed) noted in the MA, and
  * a sunset date for the exception.

- Rollout policy: Recommend A/B style canary by region (US first) with automatic fallback to Infer-V1 for requests that fail the compatibility checks. We should also expose a customer-level flag in the Console so CS can flip customers back to V1 during the transition.

Related links: I added acceptance criteria to the migration folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-infer-v2-migration (see /acceptance/).

I'll sync with Eng on cost for the extra tokenizer work and update this thread by Friday.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao

Thanks for the clear proposal, Ben. A couple operational notes and a slightly adjusted schedule based on release calendar and support coverage: 

- Proposed revised dates: customer pre-notice 2028-06-03 (Mon), public notice 2028-06-10, auto-migrate start 2028-07-08 (Mon, after a security patch window), 30-day reminder 2028-08-08. This gives Support a two-week runway after public notice to triage early asks.

- Comms ownership: Marissa drafts the notice + FAQ. Ben + CS will handle targeted outreach for top-40 accounts (Ben to own the list). Product (Aditya) to provide technical language and notable incompatibilities to include. Legal should receive the notice draft 72 hours before public send for a quick compliance check (cc: legal-team@acmeanalytics.com not needed internally, just flag for external customers).

- Exception approvals: ops suggests three approvers: PM (Aditya), Eng on-call lead (TBD), and Director-level signoff (Laura or CSM leader). I will maintain the exception tracker spreadsheet; please avoid ad-hoc email approvals — we need an auditable record.

- Risk: high-touch customers with custom integrations will need a 1:1 migration plan; recommend Ben and CS book kickoff calls this week for customers flagged in the attached spreadsheet.

I'll update the spreadsheet and lock the comms calendar by EOD Friday 2028-05-19.

Laura Bennett
